item.title: Roberto De Zerbi says Tottenham’s woeful record at Chelsea is ‘good motivation’
item.description: Roberto De Zerbi has insisted Tottenham will use their horrible record at Chelsea as motivation and not allow it to build pressure before Saturday’s London derby. Spurs have claimed only one victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League era and lost 10 of the last 12 meetings between the rival clubs. However, De Zerbi was quick to shut down any suggestions Tottenham’s poor form in this derby will add pressure and instead backed his players to build on Monday’s 3-1 home win over Coventry . Asked if he sensed any fear in his squad, De Zerbi said: “No. I think no because I play just one game with Chelsea as Tottenham coach. Anyway, it has to be one motivation more. Not one more problem for us. Roberto De Zerbi encourages his players during Tottenham’s win over Coventry (John Walton/PA). “What is the problem? We didn’t play in the past for Tottenham and I was not the Tottenham coach in the last seasons. It is not a problem. We have already many problems and this is not a problem. “I think it’s not just this negative record. There are many, many negative records, but for me it’s one motivation more. “For the players, I want this negative record, they give us more motivation, more mentality, more energy to win a game, to play a good game, because we have the qualities enough to win. “Yes, it’s a derby against one very good team, very good coach, they have a clear style of play, great players, but also Tottenham players are very good. “The level of the (Tottenham) players is high. We have to show together as a team, not as an individual.” Spurs’ efforts to claim a first win at Chelsea since 2018 are not helped by the absence of Destiny Udogie and potentially James Maddison , who marked his first start in 536 days with a goal against Coventry, but has since missed three days of training. James Maddison hit the target for Spurs against Coventry (John Walton/PA) Dejan Kulusevski has also followed an individual plan after an emotional comeback following an 18-month absence, but Pedro Porro is available after a hamstring issue and both Andy Robertson and Omar Marmoush are fine after they were forced off on Monday. “In the first three days Maddison didn’t work with us, I don’t know if he’s ready for tomorrow,” De Zerbi explained. “Like I said many times, I don’t want to take risks, because if you analyse this period of European football, you can see many injuries, not for Tottenham, for everyone. So if I can, I don’t want to take risks to lose many players for many games. “Kulusevski also. Kulusevski worked well, but in the first days he stayed individual. “With the medical staff, we are trying to find the best way for (Udogie). “After Manchester United , I have not worked with him and this is a problem. “We are lucky because we have in the same position many solutions, but we have to find the best for him and the best for us.”

item.title: Liverpool given major boost in pursuit of €60m attacker
item.description: Liverpool given major boost in pursuit of €60m attacker Liverpool's attack has been a bit of a problem for them over the last couple of years. When Jurgen Klopp was at the helm, his trio of Mohamed Salah, Roberto Firmino and Sadio Mane helped carry the Reds to their Premier League and Champions League wins. However, as they got older, they were shipped out and sent away to other clubs. And, while Salah may have stayed put until the start of the 2026-27 season, Liverpool didn't stop trying to replace the dynamic trio with £241 million being spent on Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz just last summer. At that point, most fans thought their problems would have been answered but, unfortunately, that was far from the case. This led to another £150 million + being spent on Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola which, at this point, still hasn't been enough. So, even though almost £400 million has been splashed on fixing the Reds' attack, links are still being shared with new options for Liverpool with the Anfield outfit now being handed a major boost in their pursuit of one long-term target. Arda Guler's new Real Madrid deal could open up the door for an Endrick exit Endrick has been linked with a Liverpool move for a while now. Although the Brazilian started his career as a striker, during his time with Los Blancos, he's managed to get used to playing on the right-wing. However, since Jose Mourinho has been in charge, the youngster has barely managed to feature for the La Liga outfit which has caused many questions about his future to arise. Throughout the summer, the 20-year-old was linked with many different teams but, of the lot, Liverpool's interest probably made the most sense. item.title: Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at training
item.description: Kompany was appointed Bayern Munich manager in May 2024 [Getty Images] Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club's second team train on Friday. The 40-year-old had been unwell with a virus and missed the pre-match news conference on Tuesday prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal, however, the Belgian was on the touchline for the match. "Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs," said a statement from the Bundesliga club. "The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. "Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. "For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations." Bayern's next game is against Freiburg in the German top flight on Sunday. item.title: Dan Campbell Sends Clear Message About Sam LaPorta Controversy
item.description: The Detroit Lions have spent much of the week answering questions about Sam LaPorta’s frustration with his contract situation, and now head coach Dan Campbell has weighed in. item.title: Alonso sees Courtois similarities in Chelsea's Penders
item.description: Mike Penders is set to deputise for the injured Emi Martinez (PETER POWELL) Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso sees similarities to Thibaut Courtois in Mike Penders as he backed the goalkeeper to step into the void left by Emi Martinez's injury. The 21-year-old Penders became the Blues' youngest Premier League keeper when the Belgian replaced Martinez, who has undergone surgery on a fractured jaw, during the second half of last weekend's 2-0 win away at Everton. Widely regarded as one of the best keepers in the world, Real Madrid's Courtois was a Chelsea player for a seven-year spell between 2011 and 2018, although he spent the first three seasons on loan at Atletico Madrid. Courtois also worked under Alonso during his spell in charge of Spanish giants Real Madrid. "A lot (of similarities), not just for the nationality," said Alonso of the Belgian duo of Courtois and Penders ahead of Chelsea's clash against Tottenham on Saturday. "For the stature, both left-footed, both dominant in the air. I spoke with Thibaut when he was at the World Cup, I asked him about Mike. He said himself he could see a resemblance. "We need to help him, support him. He's a keeper for the present and for the future." Chelsea agreed a deal to sign Penders two years ago but he spent the past two seasons at his previous club Genk and then on loan at Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg. "He's ready," added Alonso. "He's been training well, he's played a couple of cup games, he's shown he has a good level. "When he came on against Everton, he showed his personality, his qualities. We are fully convinced that Mike can play very well." Martinez required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last weekend. But Alonso, whose side are fourth in the Premier League and eight points behind leaders Manchester City, is hopeful the Argentina number one will not be sidelined for long. "Few weeks, hopefully less than more," said Alonso. "The good thing is he's feeling better. We need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors and specialists. "Considering that it was a bad one (injury), he's doing good." kca/jdg/bsp

item.title: Report: Bears tight end Cole Kmet’s injury is ‘likely’ season-ending
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears is carted off the field after being injured in a play against the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Cole Kmet immediately grabbed his knee after being tackled in last night’s game, I hoped he’d just taken an awkward hit and would walk it off, just as we’ve seen so often during his seven-year Chicago Bears career. Then the cart came out for him, and I hoped it would just be precautionary. But then head coach Ben Johnson met the media after the game and didn’t seem optimistic, saying it didn’t look very good. The Bears have yet to make an official statement, but according to Ian Rapoport , the NFL Insider for ESPN and NFL Network, Kmet is “believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury.” He added that Kmet will undergo more tests this morning and “until those results come back, there is no finality.” I reached out to a source to corroborate Rapoport’s report and was told it’s believed to be a torn ACL. “I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, to this organization,” Caleb Williams said about Kmet in his postgame press conference. “He’s the longest-tenured Bear, I believe. He’s been through it. So, it’s challenging; it’s tough. I’ll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole has been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, the second year, and now through this year. So, I can only do the same for him.” Kmet, drafted with the 43rd overall pick in the 2020 draft, is the longest-tenured Bear, and having grown up in suburban Lake Barrington, Illinois, as a Bears fan, he’s had Navy and Orange in his blood his whole life. Last month, Kmet wrote an article for The Player’s Tribune about his lifelong love of the Bears. I just want to win games and represent for this city, and for this team that I’ve loved since way back when I got that badass Urlacher jersey for Christmas. I want to do all I can to help bring another Lombardi Trophy home to Chicago. And hopefully we can all join together to make that happen this season, because I’d love to see all of you on Michigan Avenue for a big parade this winter if everything goes our way. Kmet did a lot of the little things on the football field to help the Bears win games, so his contributions will definitely be missed, but what he brings to the locker room as a team leader will be missed as well.

item.title: Brewers Place Brandon Woodruff On World Series Roster
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Brandon Woodruff All week, the biggest question facing the Milwaukee Brewers was whether or not Brandon Woodruff was going to make the World Series roster, and he officially has. He has not pitched in a game since July 4, when his fastball velocity was way down. He was placed on the injured list with a shoulder injury, presumed to need season-ending shoulder surgery. However, he somehow avoided surgery and started working to get back. This week, he faced hitters for the first time, and his velocity was right where he expected it to be, and all indications are that he threw the ball well. item.title: Australia come back to beat Scotland again in WXV
item.description: Piper Duck scored one of three second-half tries for Australia [Getty Images] WXV Global Series Australia (14) 38 Tries : Whitaker, Stewart, Moleka, Duck, Palu Cons : Wood 5 Pen : Wood Scotland (17) 31 Tries : Malcolm 2, Sutcliffe, Buchanan, Lloyd Cons : Nelson 3 Scotland failed to hang on to a half-time lead against Australia in Canberra as they slumped to a ninth straight Test defeat. The visitors finish their WXV Global Series campaign with five losses from five, having lost to Canada and New Zealand before three straight defeats by the Wallaroos. Dave Butcher's side shipped eight tries in their previous outing in Sydney last week and appeared on course for another bruising scoreline when converted scores from Amelia Whitaker and Maya Stewart put the hosts 14-0 up after 12 minutes. However, the beleaguered tourists responded through captain Rachel Malcolm's opportunistic try and slowly gained a measure of control. After Australia centre Cecilia Smith was sin-binned for a high tackle on Scotland full-back Chloe Rollie, Aicha Sutcliffe scored the Scots' second try at the back of a rolling maul and Helen Nelson's conversion made it a two-point game. Australia finished the half with 13 players as Waiaria Ellis joined Smith in the sin-bin and Scotland went in front soon after. Katie Buchanan skipped past two would-be tacklers to score Scotland's third try and boost hopes that a long-awaited win might be in the offing. Australia retook the lead just four minutes into the second half though. After Rollie was yellow carded, Faitala Moleka scored the home side's third try, converted by the unerring boot of Sam Wood. And things went from bad to worse for Scotland when Piper Duck's converted try made it 28-17 on 52 minutes. Rhona Lloyd hit back after a brilliant carry from Scotland number eight Evie Gallagher, but a Wood penalty and a converted try from home captain Siokapesi Palu Sekona took the game out of reach. A flurry of cards late on meant both teams finished without a full XV as Lloyd was sin-binned for denying a try-scoring opportunity and Cecilia Smith was shown her second yellow of the match for a high tackle. Malcolm dotted down for her second try late on, but it was merely a consolation. item.title: Bills' DB gets good news from NFL as suspension for spitting changed to $14,926 fine
item.description: Bills' DB gets good news from NFL as suspension for spitting changed to $14,926 fine originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In Week 6, the Buffalo Bills beat the Las Vegas Raiders , and in the game, C.J. Gardner-Johnson was caught spitting toward a Raiders player, leading to the NFL suspending him for a game. But Gardner-Johnson wasn't the only one to face a suspension from the NFL for spitting in that game. Bills defensive back Sam Franklin was also facing suspension after allegedly spitting on a Raiders player. However, ESPN's Adam Schefter shared some good news for Franklin and the Bills, as the NFL has reduced his punishment from a one-game suspension to a fine. Bills' Sam Franklin won appeal, won't be suspended "Per @NFLfootballinfo: Hearing officer James Thrash, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has reduced the discipline of Bills S Sam Franklin from a one-game suspension to a fine of $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct," Schefter shared. This is some great news for the Bills and Franklin. While he's still being punished by the NFL, in the form of a nearly $15,000 fine, he's not going to miss a game. With Gardner-Johnson's appeal not working, meaning he's suspended for the Bills' next game, getting this piece of news on Franklin is a very positive update for the Bills. MORE : Bills have another player suspended by NFL for a spitting incident vs. Raiders The Bills are on bye in Week 7, so the game Franklin was initially set to miss, and the one Gardner-Johnson will miss, is a Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens . While Gardner-Johnson is not going to play against Baltimore in Week 8, Franklin is good to go, with the NFL reducing his punishment for his unsportsmanlike conduct against the Raiders in Week 6. It's not a perfect outcome, as he's still getting a hefty fine. But being able to have Franklin on the field for Week 8 is still a very positive development for the Bills. item.title: Bayern release update on Kompany after collapse
item.description: Bayern release update on Kompany after collapse Bayern Munich have provided an update on Vincent Kompany after the Belgian coach suddenly collapsed towards the end of a training session on Friday. “Vincent Kompany had to receive medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session involving FC Bayern’s reserve team. The first-team manager had been watching the second team’s training session,” the club stated. “Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical supervision. Until further notice, his coaching staff will take charge of training sessions and matches.” Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl commented: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our highest priority. At FC Bayern, we will do everything we can to ensure that he recovers quickly. Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.” Kompany has recently been battling a viral infection and hip problems. As a result, he had to sit down during Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig last week. He also missed the final training session and pre-match press conference ahead of Wednesday’s 2-2 draw against Arsenal, but returned to the dugout to lead his team during the match.

item.title: Brighton boss Fabian Hürzeler breaks silence on Manchester United rumours, sends clear message
item.description: Brighton boss Fabian Hürzeler breaks silence on Manchester United rumours, sends clear message One topic trending across the internet is who might replace Michael Carrick if this Manchester United side continues to struggle. After the humiliating 4-1 defeat to Como, some United fans expected the club to sack him immediately. Yet Ineos chose not to act, leaving Carrick in the dugout as United prepare to face AFC Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Whether this match proves to be the turning point of his reign remains to be seen. For his sake, he will hope things finally click and he keeps his job. Should the status quo continue, however, and United go eight games without a win, Ineos will have no further excuses and will almost certainly sack him. Several excellent coaches remain linked with the job, and fans are already debating who is best placed to raise the level at Old Trafford. Those who believe Fabian Hürzeler is the man, though, are set for disappointment. Fabian Hürzeler responds to Manchester United links The Brighton & Hove Albion head coach addressed the speculation surrounding the Old Trafford hot seat in his latest press conference. “I am really focused on my job here,” Hürzeler said, as reported by Sussex World . “I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. “Besides that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and for what he achieved with Manchester United at the end of last season. He is a great human being and a great personality. Every time we meet, we enjoy a really good relationship, so I respect him deeply, and there is nothing more to say about that.” Hürzeler declines to follow Sergej Jakirović’s example It would have been intriguing had Hürzeler taken the same route as Sergej Jakirović . The Hull City manager recently made it clear that he would love the chance to coach United if the opportunity arose. He later clarified and withdrew those remarks, but the words were already out. Hürzeler, by contrast, has chosen not to stake any claim for the United job, and few can blame him. His Brighton side are flying high. They sit third in the Premier League with 16 points, have scored more goals than any other team, and boast a resilient defence that has conceded very few goals and kept four consecutive clean sheets. Premier League-proven and tactically astute, Hürzeler would have represented a major coup for United. Yet that move is clearly not happening, and his comments should give Brighton the confidence to firmly rebuff any approach for their manager.

Yet Ineos chose not to act, leaving Carrick in the dugout as United prepare to face AFC Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Whether this match proves to be the turning point of his reign remains to be seen. For his sake, he will hope things finally click and he keeps his job. Should the status quo continue, however, and United go eight games without a win, Ineos will have no further excuses and will almost certainly sack him. Several excellent coaches remain linked with the job, and fans are already debating who is best placed to raise the level at Old Trafford. Those who believe Fabian Hürzeler is the man, though, are set for disappointment. Fabian Hürzeler responds to Manchester United links The Brighton & Hove Albion head coach addressed the speculation surrounding the Old Trafford hot seat in his latest press conference. “I am really focused on my job here,” Hürzeler said, as reported by Sussex World . “I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. “Besides that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and for what he achieved with Manchester United at the end of last season. He is a great human being and a great personality. Every time we meet, we enjoy a really good relationship, so I respect him deeply, and there is nothing more to say about that.” Hürzeler declines to follow Sergej Jakirović’s example It would have been intriguing had Hürzeler taken the same route as Sergej Jakirović . The Hull City manager recently made it clear that he would love the chance to coach United if the opportunity arose. He later clarified and withdrew those remarks, but the words were already out. Hürzeler, by contrast, has chosen not to stake any claim for the United job, and few can blame him. His Brighton side are flying high. They sit third in the Premier League with 16 points, have scored more goals than any other team, and boast a resilient defence that has conceded very few goals and kept four consecutive clean sheets. Premier League-proven and tactically astute, Hürzeler would have represented a major coup for United. Yet that move is clearly not happening, and his comments should give Brighton the confidence to firmly rebuff any approach for their manager.

item.title: Dalton Knecht Signs With NBA Champion Knicks Following Lakers Cut
item.description: The New York Knicks signed former Los Angeles Lakers forward Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal Friday, per ESPN’s Shams Charania. The Lakers waived Knecht on Monday to shave their roster to 15 players after failing to get a trade across for the third-year forward. Former Lakers forward Dalton Knecht has agreed to sign with the New York Knicks on a two-way NBA contract, his agents at Excel Sports Management tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/1gePugMy3Z — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 23, 2026 The Lakers signed plenty of forward depth in the offseason to make up for their losses of LeBron James and Rui Hacimura, further reducing Knecht’s already limited role within the team. With so many players in front of him, the Lakers decided to waive him over some of their other options. Knecht had a big role in the 2024-25 season, playing in 78 of the Lakers’ 82 games averaging nearly 20 minutes on the floor. He posted 9.1 points, 2.8 rebounds and 0.8 assists per game, and figured to be a big part of the team’s future. After a trade which would have sent Knecht to the Charlotte Hornets fell through, though, his role shrunk. The 25-year-old played in 54 games for the team last year, but only started once and averaged just 10.2 minutes per game on the season. He averaged 4.2 points per game, less than half of his average from the season prior, and his efficiency dropped as a result of his reduced playing time as well. Oct 12, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers forward Dalton Knecht (4) warms up prior to the game against the Golden State Warriors at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Where Does Dalton Knecht Fit With the Knicks? With the Knicks, Knecht will look to get some playing time behind forwards Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby, and has a shot at breaking into the team. The Knicks’ staggering depth played a huge part in their NBA Championship run last year, but they lacked out-and-out forwards—predominantly using guards to fill in at small forward throughout the playoffs. Guards Josh Hart and Jordan Clarkson are their options behind Mikal Bridges, and while they’re both good players, the Knicks surely could use a traditional forward to bring in off the bench. Knecht’s next opportunity to feature for his team comes Friday, when the Knicks take on the Celtics for their second game of the season at 4:00 p.m. PT. The Lakers also resume play on Friday, facing off against the Los Angeles Clippers for their second game of the season at 7:00 p.m. PT. item.title: LeBron James claps back at Trump’s national anthem comments with zinger
item.description: LeBron James has broken his silence on President Donald Trump’s comments condemning his behavior during the National Anthem. James was seen on the court finishing warm ups as the anthem played ahead of the Philadelphia 76ers’ Tuesday night showdown against the reigning NBA Champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Footage showed James stretching his arms and loosening his torso, appearing to mimic a golf swing. Trump wasted no time sharing a video of James in the moment, along with a rant on Truth Social: “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” James clapped back after Philadelphia’s Thursday night home opener and comeback win over his former team, the Cleveland Cavaliers, dropping a zingy one-liner when asked about Trump’s comments. “It’s a slow news day at the office, you know. Slow news day in the office,” James told reporters. LeBron James has clapped back at Donald Trump (Reuters) 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said Trump’s comments were “right in with all the other outside noise we’ve already had.” “All I really care about is getting them to the practice floor, getting in the film room, getting them to the game floor. And the focus that they’ve had and the intent and all the stuff they’ve had has been excellent,” Nurse said. James and Trump have publicly exchanged barbs dating back to 2017 when the four-time NBA MVP called the president a “bum” after his White House rescinded an invitation to the Golden State Warriors. James followed up by saying that a visit to Washington, D.C. was an honor “until you showed up.” The Independent has reached out to the White House for comment. James made his 76ers home debut Thursday night (Getty) The exchange follows James’s debut with the Philadelphia 76ers after opting to extend his career during the off-season by signing with the team. James helped the 76ers to a Tuesday night win over the reigning champion Knicks, 106-100. He scored 14 points in 34 minutes on the court. He followed that up Thursday with a come-from-behind win over the Cavaliers, 114-106. Speaking to NBC after Tuesday’s game, James said: “I could be a lot better. Still getting my rhythm, obviously just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad. “But I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well.”

item.title: Replica trophy held by iconic player after World Cup win heads for auction
item.description: After the 2022 World Cup in Qatar which Argentina won, the winning team, including captain Lionel Messi, passed a replica trophy around. That trophy is going to be part an auction scheduled for Nov. 7, organized by South Carolina-based Richmond Auctions. The company said the trophy was used during the post-match on-field celebration. It was subsequently autographed by members of Argentina’s championship squad and exhibited at the National Historical Museum of Buenos Aires in Argentina. The trophy is paired with a trading card depicting Messi carrying the replica trophy after Argentina defeated France at the 2022 World Cup. “Together, these two collectibles represent a unique opportunity to acquire both an autographed artifact from Argentina’s championship celebration and a pristine trading card depicting that very moment,” per the auction house. “A truly special pairing celebrating one of the most memorable achievements in international football history.” The company said the trophy is accompanied by duly translated and legalized notarial instruments, together with photographs and videos documenting its authenticity and traceability. Jordan Richmond, co-founder of Richmond Auctions, said, “What drew us to this piece is the same point that draws us to exceptional collectibles across every category: rarity, provenance and a story that can’t be recreated.” Read the original article on NJ.com . The Spanish side celebrated their first-ever win on Scottish soil in their 55-year European history, with their debut also being in Scotland, against Aberdeen. item.title: NFL insists on playing Steelers-Saints Paris game despite ongoing riots
item.description: The NFL’s insistence on playing around the globe has led the league to France this weekend. However, the ongoing Paris riots are creating a very unstable situation ahead of the Pittsburgh Steelers-New Orleans Saints game. Sunday’s Week 7 games are slated to kick off with the Steelers and Saints contest. That’s if the league is able to continue on with its current plans. Unrest in France’s capital city has led to major soccer team Paris Saint-Germain postponing their Sunday match at the request of local police. The defending UEFA Champions League winners will play their game against Lyon on Monday, per The Athletic . Paris has seen an increase in riots over recent weeks as protesters remain upset with president Emmanuel Macron. Many residents and students cite rising cost of living, as well as demands for better education and school conditions. Meanwhile, the NFL seemingly has no plans to pivot heading into the Steelers-Saints contest. The league maintains that enhanced security will be enough to deal with the current issues in Paris. That could be risky though given the nature of the ongoing riots. MORE: Should NFL reconsider international game scheduling in light of recent issues? Does the NFL have a backup plan? NFL commissioner Roger Goodell greets fans before the game between Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) As Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio points out, the NFL already plays a lot of international games in Europe. It’s unideal to move the matchup at this stage, but it certainly seems feasible considering the potential risk the league is taking on. The NFL just spent the last three weeks hosting games in England at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Wembley Stadium. Neither stadium is in use for the upcoming weekend, creating a potential fallback option for commissioner Roger Goodell and Co. There’s a very small chance the NFL would reschedule the game for the future considering the league’s been down this road before. The COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and major field concerns in Brazil earlier this season for the Baltimore Ravens’ win against the Dallas Cowboys created uncertainty over holding games. MORE: 4 NFL international cities deserving of franchises Ultimately, games are very rarely postponed in the NFL. item.title: MSU’s D line took a big step. Now, it’s on teammates to follow
item.description: EAST LANSING — No group, defensive coordinator Joe Rossi says, has made quite as big a leap as his defensive line has seven games into the 2026 season. Being that the past five have been losses, though, the task falls on every other room to follow suit. Michigan State’s coaching staff is hopeful that midseason growth from a previously struggling position room can serve as inspiration for the rest of the Spartans (2-5, 0-4 Big Ten), who take a five-game losing streak to No. 10 UCLA (6-0, 4-0) this Saturday, Oct. 24, for a bout at the Rose Bowl. In Monday morning’s team meeting, coaches used the defensive line’s growth as an example for teammates to follow. “I pulled up a bunch of plays and I had too many,” MSU coach Pat Fitzgerald said Oct. 19. Imagine if you told Fitzgerald that a week ago. Through the first six games of the season, Michigan State had mustered just seven sacks, and four of those came Week 2 against Eastern Michigan . The Spartans didn’t record a sack in their first three Big Ten games against Nebraska, at Wisconsin and against Illinois. It wasn’t just bad luck. Fundamentally, the group did a bad job of setting edges and creating vertical pressure. Even lining up on the ball, they ceded a whole yard to the opposition. That defensive line then exploded for five sacks against Northwestern this past Saturday, Oct. 17. A pair each went to nose tackle Ben Roberts and edge rusher Anelu Lafaele, the former who is playing like an All-Big Ten caliber player in the eyes of his coaches and the latter who finally looks himself athletically after an injury last season. Defensive lineman Eli Coenen and edge rusher Keahnist Thompson also shared a sack. More: Even in a losing season, Michigan State will still get to play in Rose Bowl The problem is the scoreboard: 24-21. Northwestern won the game in the final minute on an eight-play, 64-yard field goal drive after blocking the Spartans’ own attempt. “We’ve been talking about how we need to just continue to get after it and work our plan,” Coenen said Oct. 21. “So for us, we just gotta keep working. That game’s behind us now.” Both Fitzgerald and Rossi credited the pass rush’s growth to energetic coaching from defensive line coach Winston DeLattiboudere III — DeBo for short — and rush ends coach Andrew Bindelglass. We wanted it… From a month ago, we thought we had a deal. I think you need to talk to the Temple AD and get your stories right. This is not a Villanova thing. Villanova wants to be in the Big 5. They are the Big 5. But unfortunately, either people are illiterate, which I don’t think they are, or you’re just a bad writer.” When Neiburg asked whether Villanova wanted to keep the current format, Willard called it “stupid.” He said he had pushed for a Hall of Fame banquet the night before the Classic, which he claimed the other schools couldn’t afford, along with a schedule that built more predictably toward the tripleheader. “The other schools couldn’t afford it, supposedly, or didn’t want to do it,” Willard said of the banquet. “And then I wanted the games to lead up to the Xfinity game. I wanted to have continuity and the fact that people would know when we’re playing, so that we can actually get people to the games. We played La Salle and there was 500 people. You know, Penn played Saint Joe’s and there’s 2,000 people. My whole thing was I just wanted to make it the way it was, but the other schools didn’t see it the same way.” Willard then explained the format Villanova had wanted, which Neiburg’s sources described as giving the two teams with the highest NET rankings from the previous season a bye and a home game heading into the Classic. Multiple sources told Neiburg, however, that Temple was far from the only school unwilling to approve it. In regards to Kevin Willard blaming Temple: according to multiple sources, Temple wasn’t the only school that wasn’t going to sign off on the format that Villanova wanted. — Jeff Neiburg (@Jeff_Neiburg) October 23, 2026 Willard also suggested Neiburg’s reporting mentioned Villanova only to drive traffic, claiming nobody would have clicked on the story otherwise. “I know the only way he could get clicks is to put Villanova in it, because if they didn’t put Villanova, no one would click on his article,” Willard said. “… Your own headline says it. I’m still perplexed that people didn’t read your article. I’m not perplexed. I now know why. But it says that the five other schools decided to opt out. It wasn’t Villanova. Villanova was all in. They opted out.” The headline did say the five other schools were moving forward with a round-robin format without Villanova in 2027-28, because that’s exactly what they announced, and the story underneath it laid out why, explaining that Villanova had no interest in keeping the current format and that its alternative would have all but guaranteed the Wildcats never played another Big 5 road game. “So talk to the other schools,” Willard said. “This is not a Villanova issue. The other schools opted out. They didn’t want to play us.” Full disclosure: I’m a Temple graduate. But you don’t need Cherry and White tinted glasses to see that Willard’s version of events doesn’t hold up against his own words. In June 2025, only a few months after taking the Villanova job, Willard told the Inquirer that an annual Atlantic 10 road game was an undue burden for a team already playing 20 Big East games, and that surrendering a home date was costly at a time when revenue had become paramount. Sixteen months later, he swore Villanova had been “all in” on the Big 5 and “didn’t opt out,” even though his school’s proposal was custom-built to resolve the very grievances he aired before he ever coached a Big 5 game. Despite all his talk Thursday night about loving the Big 5 and being “all in,” Willard never set out to preserve a 70-year-old tradition so much as reshape it into something that served Villanova’s bottom line. From the outset, Villanova sought an arrangement that would all but ensure the Wildcats hosted their Big 5 games and never again had to make the trip to North Broad Street, Olney, or Hawk Hill. And when the other five schools refused to play ball, he recast himself — and his school — as the aggrieved party desperately trying to hold the Big 5 together. Villanova’s athletic department now faces the task of salvaging its standing with five neighboring schools after its basketball coach publicly scapegoated one of their athletic directors and derided another school’s fan base. People who had no part in Thursday’s tirade, including Denise Dillon, whose women’s program is still expected to compete in the Big 5 alongside all five schools, will have to do much of the work to mend those relationships, according to Neiburg. Willard was hired to win Big East games and chase national titles, and nothing about his contemptible press conference diminishes his ability to do either. It did show, however, how little regard he has for the parts of the job that require him to be a good neighbor, and Villanova will pay for that long after this season’s Classic. In fact, the bill has already come due on the football side, where a 2027 game against Temple that had been in the works is no longer happening, Awful Announcing has learned. item.title: Four-time Pro Bowler wants New York Giants to get Derrick Henry like talent to the roster
item.description: Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images Former Los Angeles Rams tackle Andrew Whitworth has suggested the New York Giants to add Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor to their roster. Since the firing of Colts General Manager Chris Ballard, there have been reports that Taylor could be on his way out of the team just months after signing a two-year $44 million extension. One of the reasons Taylor has been in trade talks is the poor form the Colts are in. Yet again, they have started the season poorly, but this time with CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon heavily involved, some wholesale changes are going to be made to the roster. Multiple teams have expressed interest in Taylor, but Andrew Whitworth believes the New York Giants should be the franchise that goes all in for the three-time Pro Bowler. Andrew Whitworth believes Jonathan Taylor can bring Derrick Henry-like effect to the Giants The Giants are navigating through RB problems of their own, as John Harbaugh limited the involvement of Cam Skattebo in the Giants’ loss to the New Orleans Saints. He did not have a single touch or carry due to his poor performance against the Washington Commanders. However, Whitworth’s reason behind bringing a player like Taylor is a bit different. “You think of that running back situation, they’re very unhappy with. What has John Harbaugh done since he came from Baltimore, he’s brought a whole lot of Baltimore influence into that team with players and everything else, could he go get his Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor, bring Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants, get your Derrick Henry physical runner, a guy who can be explosive take it to the house, to me that would be the move I look for if I was the New York Giants, let’s find our Derrick Henry and give it to John Harbaugh,” said Whitworth on TNF. While Taylor has not yet achieved what Henry has in the league, there is no doubt that the Colts player is among the best RBs in the league. This season, he has already recorded 492 rushing yards and is second in the league in rushing touchdowns. Having spent his entire career in Indianapolis, he has gone to the postseason only once, which shows that he hasn’t had a good supporting cast around him. If he moves to the Giants, Taylor will be playing under Harbaugh, who made the Ravens one of the best teams in the AFC. Henry played two seasons with Harbaugh and was brilliant under the legendary coach. He finished second in rushing yards in both those seasons. This shows that Harbaugh’s system is well-suited for players who are explosive and strong, both qualities even Taylor possesses. It is still unclear where the Colts stand on letting their star RB go. If they decide to clear house and rebuild, Taylor is definitely a player who will fetch them a huge haul, which is why they might be interested in trading him away, especially to a team like the Giants, who are looking to strengthen their team. United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
